text:
The primary material of a candle is wax.

The city at night is a canvas of light, each skyscraper a brushstroke of vibrant fluorescence against the deep indigo of the twilight sky, painting an urban masterpiece that wakes up as the rest of the world sleeps. In this nocturnal gallery, the wax of a candle is the silent architect of intimacy, a solidified pool of memory waiting to be melted by the spark of attention. Like a frozen tear of the sun, it holds the potential for warmth and illumination, transforming from a rigid, opaque block into a fluid vessel of guidance. Just as the skyscrapers pierce the sky with electric ambition, the candle pierces the darkness with a humble, flickering truth, its flame a tiny, dancing star that reminds us that even the smallest source of light can carve a path through the deepest indigo of the unknown.
